events.title: Bill of Rights Ratified
events.description: Virginia became the necessary tenth state to ratify the first ten amendments to the U.S. Constitution, known collectively as the Bill of Rights, making them part of the law of the land.
events.significance: The Bill of Rights guarantees fundamental individual liberties such as freedom of speech, religion, press, and assembly, and protections against government overreach, forming a cornerstone of American constitutional democracy.

events.title: Death of Sitting Bull
events.description: Lakota Sioux leader Sitting Bull was killed at the Standing Rock Reservation in South Dakota during an attempt by Indian agency police to arrest him amid fears he would join the Ghost Dance movement.
events.significance: His death heightened tensions on the Plains and contributed to the Wounded Knee Massacre two weeks later, marking the end of armed Native American resistance on the Great Plains.

events.title: Premiere of Gone with the Wind
events.description: The epic film Gone with the Wind, based on Margaret Mitchell's novel, held its world premiere in Atlanta, Georgia, with a large public celebration.
events.significance: The film went on to win ten Academy Awards and became one of the highest-grossing films of all time when adjusted for inflation, though it is also now widely discussed for its romanticized portrayal of the antebellum South and slavery.

events.title: Adolf Eichmann Sentenced to Death
events.description: An Israeli court in Jerusalem sentenced Adolf Eichmann, a principal organizer of the Holocaust, to death after his trial for crimes against humanity and crimes against the Jewish people.
events.significance: The trial brought the horrors of the Holocaust to worldwide attention, shaped debates on international justice and individual responsibility, and inspired Hannah Arendt's concept of the 'banality of evil.'

events.title: Glenn Miller Disappears
events.description: Bandleader and U.S. Army Air Forces Major Glenn Miller disappeared when his plane vanished over the English Channel while flying from England to Paris to prepare for a performance for troops.
events.significance: Miller was one of the best-selling musicians of the Swing Era, and his unexplained disappearance became one of World War II's enduring mysteries, marking the loss of an iconic figure in American popular music.
